name: Beta-alanine
short: Paraesthesia (tingling) was the only side effect reported in a risk assessment of 101 human studies, far more often than with placebo; a small rise in a liver enzyme stayed within normal ranges.
text: A systematic risk assessment and meta-analysis covering 101 human and 50 animal studies of isolated oral beta-alanine found that paraesthesia (tingling) was the only reported side effect, with estimated odds 8.9 times those with placebo, while dropout rates were similar in active and placebo groups. The same analysis found a small increase in circulating alanine aminotransferase, a liver enzyme, although mean values remained well within clinical reference ranges, and concluded that beta-alanine at the doses used in the available research does not adversely affect those taking it. A sports nutrition position stand likewise states that beta-alanine currently appears to be safe in healthy populations at recommended doses and that paraesthesia is the only reported side effect. A more cautious evidence review for military personnel noted that most studies were not designed to address safety and rated the strength of evidence for a causal relation between beta-alanine and paraesthesia as moderate. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
